utility.notes: Concord's own Community Choice Energy (MCE) page confirms: 'the existing electrical utility, PG&E, delivers that power, continuing the metering and billing for customers.' PG&E is the underlying transmission/distribution/billing utility; MCE is a separate default generation supplier — see generation_supplier.

value.name: MCE (Marin Clean Energy) - Light Green (default service)
value.notes: Concord's own page states MCE 'began providing the City of Concord with an alternative to PG&E' in 2018, and that customers who take no action are 'automatically enrolled in MCE's "Light Green" power supply, which is made up of 50% renewable power' as the default, with 'Deep Green' (100% renewable) and 'Local Sol' (100% local solar) available as opt-up choices.

county.notes: Concord's own MCE page identifies MCE as 'Contra Costa County's community-based electricity provider' in the context of Concord's own enrollment, structurally confirming the city-county relationship; no single page was found this session stating the relationship as one direct standalone sentence.

permit_authority.value: City of Concord Building Division (Community and Economic Development Department)

interconnection_url.notes: Same PG&E-wide Net Energy Metering program URL already verified for the Fremont/Oakland/Berkeley/Richmond records — reused as a utility-level fact. pge.com returns HTTP 403 to automated fetch; confirmed to exist via search engine indexing under its expected title.

value.name: SGIP - Residential Solar and Storage Equity
value.administrator: Pacific Gas and Electric Company (PG&E), under the CPUC's Self-Generation Incentive Program
value.description: Storage incentive of $1,100/kWh paired with a solar incentive of $3,100/kW, funded via a $280 million CPUC-authorized budget that opened for reservations June 2, 2025. Administered by PG&E across its entire distribution territory, which includes Concord/Contra Costa County.
value.eligibility: PG&E or SCE residential customers (general market tier)

battery_programs.notes: Same statewide CPUC/PG&E-administered SGIP program already verified for other PG&E-territory records this session, reused here as a utility-level fact since PG&E's distribution role in Concord is independently confirmed (S2).

required_documents.notes: Concord's Solar PV Projects page references a 'Solar Permitting Checklist (PDF)' and a 'Solar PV Standardized Permit Submittal Instructions (PDF)' but neither document's contents could be located/rendered as readable text this session.

timeline_days.notes: No review/approval timeframe is stated on Concord's Solar PV Projects page. California's AB 2188 model ordinance requires an expedited timeframe be codified, but the specific municipal code chapter was not located/read this session.

eligibility_constraints.notes: Concord's Solar PV Projects page describes SolarAPP+, standard design documents, and standardized-configuration pathways but does not itself state system-size caps or property-type scope. Left null rather than assuming the common 10kW AC/single-family-duplex pattern seen in other cities without direct confirmation for Concord specifically.
